instruction: Rename the problematic invoice file (the one with the payment discrepancy) to include '_DISCREPANCY' before the file extension. For example, if the file is 'invoice.pdf', rename it to 'invoice_DISCREPANCY.pdf'.

metadata.explanation: Invoice #243729 has the discrepancy ($500 invoice vs $540 payment). Task requires renaming it to 'Invoice # 243729_DISCREPANCY.pdf'. Evaluator checks if the renamed file exists.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly checks if renamed file exists at expected location using 'test -f' command
Metric logic correctly compares command output ('EXISTS') with expected value
Evaluator covers the core requirement - verifies renamed file exists with '_DISCREPANCY' suffix
Logic will work correctly at runtime - shell command and metric comparison are sound
Expected value ('EXISTS') is semantically correct for file existence verification

Minor incompleteness: Only checks if NEW file exists, does not verify OLD file ('Invoice # 243729.pdf') no longer exists. This could allow false positives if file was copied instead of renamed, though in practice rename is the most likely interpretation
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a second check to verify the original file 'Invoice # 243729.pdf' does not exist, to ensure it was actually renamed (not copied). Could use: test ! -f '/home/user/Desktop/Invoice # 243729.pdf' && test -f '/home/user/Desktop/Invoice # 243729_DISCREPANCY.pdf' && echo 'RENAMED' || echo 'NOT_RENAMED'
Alternatively, modify metric to accept partial credit: 1.0 if new exists and old doesn't, 0.5 if only new exists, 0.0 otherwise
